THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 11 OF 1984
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 1st December, 1984]
No. F. 17 (2)/84‑Pub.‑The
following Order, made by the President, is hereby published for general
information.
Now, therefore, in pursuance of
the Provisional Constitution Order, 1981 (C. M. L. A. Order No. 1 of 1981), and
in exercise of all powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is pleased
to make the following Order :‑
THE SCHEDULE
(See Article 6)
1. Persons qualified to vote at referendum.‑Every citizen of
Pakistan who is enrolled as a voter on an electoral roll maintained under the
Electoral Rolls Act, 1974 (XXI of 1974), shall be entitled to vote at the
referendum.
2. Hours of poll.‑Poll for the purpose of the referendum
shall be taken on the 19th December, 1984, from 8.00 a. m. to 4.30 p. m.
3. Poll by secret ballot.‑The poll under this Order shall be
by secret ballot and every voter shall cast his vote by means of a ballot paper
which shall be in such form as may be prescribed.
Explanation.‑In this paragraph and the succeeding paragraphs
of this Schedule, "prescribed" means prescribed by the Commission in
such manner as it may deem fit.
4. Postal ballot.‑(I) The following persons may cast their
votes by postal ballot in such manner as the Commission may specify, namely :‑
(a) a person who is in the
service of Pakistan or holds any public office and is posted in an electoral
area other than that in which he is enrolled.
(b) the wife and children of any
such person as is referred to in clause (a), if they ordinarily reside with
such person ;
(c) a person who is detained in
prison or held in other custody in an electoral area other than that in which
he is enrolled ; and
(d) a person appointed by the
Returning Officer, including police personnel, for the performance of any duty
in connection with the referendum at a polling station other than that at which
he is entitled to cast his vote.
(2) A voter who, being entitled
to do so, intends to cast his vote by postal ballot shall‑
(a) in the case of a person
referred to in clause (a) or clause (b) or clause (c) of sub‑paragraph
(1), within such time as may be specified by the Commission ; and
(b) in the case of a person
referred to in clause (d) of sub‑paragraph (1), as soon as may be after
his appointment,
apply to the Returning Officer
for a ballot paper for voting by postal ballot ; and every such application
shall specify the name of the voter, his address and his serial number in the
electoral roll.
(3) The Returning Officer shall
immediately upon the receipt of an application by a vote under sub‑paragraph
(2) send by post to such voter a ballot paper and an envelope bearing on its
face a form of certificate of posting, showing the date thereof, to be filled in
by the proper official of the Post Office at the time of posting by the voter.
(4) A voter on receiving his
ballot paper for voting by postal ballot shall record his vote in the manner
specified by the Commission and, after so recording, post the ballot paper to
the Returning Officer in the envelope sent to him under sub‑paragraph
(3), so as to reach the Returning Officer before the consolidation of results
by him.
5. Voting procedure.‑‑‑(1) Where a voter presents
himself to vote, the presiding officer shall issue a ballot paper to him after
satisfying himself about the identity of the voter and shall, for that purpose,
require the voter to produce the identity card issued to him under the National
Registration Act, 1973 (LVI of 1973).
(2) Before a ballot paper is
issued to a voter‑
(a) a mark shall be placed on the
list of voters against the name of the voter to indicate that a ballot paper
has been issued to him ;
(b) the ballot paper shall on its
back be stamped with the official mark and initialled by the Presiding Officer
; and
(c) the voter shall put his
signature or thumb‑impression on the counterfoil.

ballot paper shall‑

Short title, extent and commencement

THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 11 OF 1984
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 1st December, 1984]
No. F. 17 (2)/84‑Pub.‑The
following Order, made by the President, is hereby published for general
information.
Now, therefore, in pursuance of
the Provisional Constitution Order, 1981 (C. M. L. A. Order No. 1 of 1981), and
in exercise of all powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is pleased
to make the following Order :‑
1. Short title, extent and commencement.‑(1) This Order may
be called the Referendum Order, 1984.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Question to be referred to a referendum

THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 11 OF 1984
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 1st December, 1984]
No. F. 17 (2)/84‑Pub.‑The
following Order, made by the President, is hereby published for general
information.
Now, therefore, in pursuance of
the Provisional Constitution Order, 1981 (C. M. L. A. Order No. 1 of 1981), and
in exercise of all powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is pleased
to make the following Order :‑
4. Question to be referred to a referendum:‑The question ;
"Whether the people of
Pakistan endorse the process initiated by General Mohammad Zia‑ul‑Haq,
the President of Pakistan, for bringing the laws of Pakistan in conformity with
the Injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah of the Holy
Prophet (peace be upon him) and for the preservation of the Ideology of
Pakistan, for the continuation and con solidation of that process and for the
smooth and orderly transfer of power to the elected representatives of the
people."
shall be referred to a referendum
on the 19th day of December, 1984.

Consequence of declaration of the result

THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 11 OF 1984
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 1st December, 1984]
No. F. 17 (2)/84‑Pub.‑The
following Order, made by the President, is hereby published for general
information.
Now, therefore, in pursuance of
the Provisional Constitution Order, 1981 (C. M. L. A. Order No. 1 of 1981), and
in exercise of all powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is pleased
to make the following Order :‑
7. Consequence of declaration of the result.‑If majority of
the votes cast in the referendum is in favour of the answer "Yes",
the people of Pakistan shall be deemed to have endorsed all steps taken by the
President of Pakistan for bringing the laws of Pakistan in conformity with the
Injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah of the Holy
Prophet (peace be upon him) and for the preservation of the Ideology of
Pakistan and for the continuation and consolidation of that process and for the
smooth and orderly transfer of power to the elected representatives of the
people ; and General Muhammad Zia‑ul‑Haq shall be deemed to have
been duly elected President of Pakistan for a term of five years from the day
of the first meeting of the Houses of Parliament in joint sitting.

Bar of jurisdiction

THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
THE REFERENDUM ORDER, 1984
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 11 OF 1984
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 1st December, 1984]
No. F. 17 (2)/84‑Pub.‑The
following Order, made by the President, is hereby published for general
information.
Now, therefore, in pursuance of
the Provisional Constitution Order, 1981 (C. M. L. A. Order No. 1 of 1981), and
in exercise of all powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is pleased
to make the following Order :‑
8. Bar of jurisdiction. No Court, including the superior Courts,
tribunal or other authority shall call in question, or permit to be called in
question, the validity of any provision of this Order or of anything done or
action taken, or purporting to be done or taken thereunder on any ground
whatsoever or grant an injunction, make any order or entertain any proceedings
in respect of any matter provided for in this Order or arising thereunder.

9. Dispute as to result of referrendum.‑All disputes as to
the result of the referendum shall be finally decided by the Commission and no
Court, including the superior Courts, or other authority shall have any
jurisdiction to entertain any proceedings relating thereto.
